ambiguities: step 1/4.a.i.2 'entries'/'maxEntries': counts distinct [context, next-symbol] pairs (literal, default entries_mode='pairs'); a non-literal variant counting distinct contexts is exposed as entries_mode='contexts' for differential diagnosis only
step 4.b.i tie rule 'the greatest y': the numerically greatest symbol value
step 4.d: a Null prediction is not equal to s_i, so it leaves correct = 0 and ends a run (the worked example shows this at i = 3, 4); D-4 records that NIST's code differed

step 4.e.i.2: 'scoreboard_winner' is read live inside the d loop, so a tie goes to the larger d and winner can change several times in one step; 6.3.7's worked example requires this reading of the identical wording, 6.3.9's example cannot distinguish it
step 8 'k': 2**bits_per_symbol (the submitter-specified output space, default) vs the number of distinct symbols observed (k_mode='observed')
step 6 '2.576' is a printed rounding of the 0.995 normal quantile; the text's constant is the default (z=2.576), the exact binary64 quantile is a variant (z=Z_BINARY64)
step 7 'binary search': bounds and tolerance unstated; [0,1] to binary64 resolution here
step 1 with L <= 2 gives N <= 0: undefined, returned as NaN
step 6 with N = 1 and P_global = 1 (L = 3, s1 = s2 = s3) divides 0 by N - 1 = 0: undefined, returned as NaN; any other L = 3 input has P_global = 0 and P'_global = 0.99
Appendix G.2 Table 3 is labelled 'L = 1 000 000' but step 7 uses N = L - 2; at the table's 4 printed decimals the two are indistinguishable
